<details class="nhsuk-details">
<summary class="nhsuk-details__summary"><span class="nhsuk-details__summary-text">Text description of this diagram</span></summary>
<div class="nhsuk-details__text">

A yellow question at the top left asks: was the change expected? An arrow marked yes goes right to a green box: a revision, which is expected and is not an error. An arrow marked no goes down to a wide blue box: a correction, which is an error, graded by what it does to the conclusions already drawn. Three arrows go down from it, one to each grade.

| The error | What happens |
|---|---|
| **Significant**, where the change would contradict the conclusions previously drawn from the data | A prominent alert on the website, corrected as soon as possible, and communicated to users and stakeholders |
| **Minor but significant**, insubstantial but warranting immediate correction in professional judgement | The published release is amended and the revision is clearly identified in it |
| **Minor but insignificant**, where a correction would reasonably be deemed inconsequential | Corrected at the next scheduled release rather than immediately |

: The three grades of error, and what happens for each

</div>
</details>
